transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’m just not sleeping right anymore. I’ll lay there at night, and if I hear rain or start thinking about the bluff giving way, I can’t shut it off. Then when I do finally fall asleep, I wake up sweaty from dreams. I’m going into work at the call center feeling like I didn’t sleep at all.
You mentioned waking up sweaty from dreams, are these dreams disturbing or frightening?

Yeah… they’re pretty frightening. I’ll finally pass out, and then I wake up sweating from them. It feels tied to the rain or thinking about that bluff giving way, and after that I’m just up, like I never really slept at all.
How long have you been experiencing these sleep problems?
It’s been about four months now. It started after I got trapped when the bluff trail collapsed, and it hasn’t really let up since.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things, beyond just the bluff giving way?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get stressed about normal stuff like work sometimes, but it’s not like I’m worrying about everything all day. It’s mostly when something reminds me of that situation.
Do you find yourself avoiding places, activities, or conversations that remind you of the bluff trail collapse?
Yeah, I do. I won’t go near the coast trails anymore, and I’ve been ignoring texts from my hiking buddies. Even just talking about going back out there makes my chest tighten.
Do you ever find yourself reliving the bluff trail collapse as if it were happening again?

Yeah… sometimes it kind of hits me out of nowhere. Like I’ll hear the sound of rocks sliding in my head, or feel like my leg is stuck under me again, and for a minute it’s like I’m back on that trail instead of sitting at my desk with my headset on.
Has your experience with the bluff trail collapse and the symptoms you've been having affected your relationships with friends or family?

Yeah, it has. I’ve kind of pulled away from my hiking friends, especially the ones who still want to go out on trails. I avoid their messages sometimes because I don’t want to talk about it or explain why I’m not going.

And it’s affected other stuff too. At work I’ve been slipping—I missed important notes in the CRM and got written up after a call escalated. I was hoping to move toward team lead, and now I’m worried I messed that up. I’ve also fallen behind on studying for my GED because I’m just tired and not keeping up like I should.
Do you find yourself jumping or getting startled more easily than you used to, even by small things that wouldn't have bothered you before?
I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I get tense sometimes, but I haven’t noticed myself jumping at small noises or anything like that more than before.
Do you try to avoid thinking about the bluff trail collapse or memories of what happened during that time?

Yeah, I do. I try not to think about it, and I avoid stuff that brings it up. I won’t go near the coast trails now, and when my hiking buddies text me, I’ll dodge it because even talking about going out there makes my chest tighten.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy before the bluff trail collapse?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t do some things like I used to, but I don’t know if it’s that I lost interest or just… I don’t feel up to it sometimes. I haven’t really thought about it that way.
Have you felt like your symptoms have significantly impacted your ability to function at work or maintain relationships?

Yeah… it has. At work I’ve been slipping. I missed some important CRM notes, and after a call got escalated I ended up getting written up. I was hoping to maybe move toward a team lead spot, and now I’m worried I messed that up.

And outside of work, I’m behind on studying for my GED because I’m just tired all the time, and I’ve been avoiding the people I used to hike with. So yeah, it’s been affecting things.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy doing before the bluff trail collapse?

I’m still not totally sure. I don’t do some of the same stuff anymore, but I can’t tell if I’ve actually lost interest or if I’m just avoiding it or don’t feel like dealing with it. I haven’t really sorted that out.
Have you felt like you're unable to perform daily tasks or maintain your usual level of productivity because of these symptoms?

Yeah. I mean, I’m still getting through some things, but not like I used to. At work I’ve slipped up enough that I missed important CRM notes, and then a call got escalated and I got written up for it. That really shook me, because I was hoping to maybe move toward a team lead role, and now I feel like I might’ve blown that.

And outside work, I’m behind on studying for my GED because I’m just exhausted. I’ve also been avoiding the people I used to hike with, so I’m not really keeping up with things the way I was.
Do you often feel guilty or ashamed about what happened during the bluff trail collapse?

Yeah… most days I do. I feel scared and embarrassed, even when nothing’s happening right then. It’s like it’s always kind of sitting there underneath everything.

And I keep thinking people can tell I messed up somehow, or that I’m not as tough as I used to act like I was. It’s hard to shake that feeling.
Have you found that you no longer enjoy or look forward to things that were previously important or pleasurable to you?

I don’t know if I’d say I no longer enjoy things. It’s more like I don’t look forward to them the same way, or I avoid making plans because I’m not sure how I’ll feel. Some stuff just feels harder to get into now, but I can’t tell if that’s because I stopped caring or because I’m just worn out by it.
Have you noticed yourself participating less in activities that were once important to you since the bluff trail collapse?
Yeah. I don’t go near the coast trails anymore. And I’ve been dodging texts from the people I used to hike with, because even just talking about going back out there makes my chest tighten.
